text:
tara: quick follow-up to the RFC — proposing a "synthetic perturbation" stage for lowbit canaries to catch failure modes that never appear in natural traffic
anjan: curious, what kinds of perturbations are you thinking? adversarial prompts? tokenization edgecases?
tara: short list: 1) random unicode/noise injections, 2) prompt truncation/concat edgecases, 3) repeated token hallucinations, 4) temperature / length stress sequences
frank: also add rare-token-heavy queries and codeblock nesting. our FP8 regressions often show up there
nina: nice. how do we generate those at scale without blowing canary budget? sampling is the real cost
tara: idea: maintain a tiny synthetic corpus (~5k samples) per model-family. run these in shadow-mode during canary sampling at 1% of traffic equivalents. cheap but targeted
frank: can we reuse shadow-sampling infra? i.e. run them through the same path but mark telemetry so ops ignores latency SLOs
anjaN: @frank +1. we should prefix with metadata so runtime can short-circuit batching heuristics: `X-Quant-Check: synthetic`
tara: example header we'll use: ```
X-Quant-Check: synthetic
X-Quant-Seed: <id>
```
nina: what's the gating logic? how do we decide to rollback vs promote? need crisp numbers for product
tara: propose: 1) quality delta metric = composite of perplexity delta, logprob drop, and token-level disagreement score. 2) if composite > threshold T_high => immediate rollback; if between T_low and T_high => hold + extended shadow for 24h
frank: define numbers: T_high = 15% composite degradation, T_low = 5%? those feel arbitrary
nina: product asks for concrete thresholds per endpoint type (chat vs code vs embeddings). we should map by workload class
anjan: operationally: create a table in the canary config: `synthetic_check: {weight: 0.01, thresholds: {chat: {low:0.05,high:0.15}, code: {...}}}`
tara: that's the plan. also we need explainability hooks — when synthetic fails, surface the sample + token diffs in Console under "Canary Synthetic Alerts"
frank: we must avoid false positives from normalization differences. add normalization step: same tokenizer, same preproc used in production model build
anjan: telemetry cost: each synthetic run is ~1x tokens of the sample. at 5k samples per model-family, at 1% load-equivalent we'll add ~50k tokens/day. negligible for hosted, but on Dedicated customers we need opt-in
nina: right — default off for Dedicated unless customer opts into "enhanced canary". good call
tara: rollout plan: 1) prototype against two small models this week; 2) bake into canary runner next sprint; 3) enable shadow flag for internal tenants; 4) widen after 2 successful weeks
frank: implementation note — plumb in existing shadow harness under eng-runtime; create `synthetic_profiles/` repo dir with generation scripts and seed lists
anjan: can we auto-generate perturbations via template rules + a tiny adversarial mutator? e.g. python script: ```
mutate(prompt):
  if rand()<0.2: insert_unicode_noise()
  if rand()<0.1: truncate_mid()
  return prompt
```
frank: love it. add a constraint to keep semantic intent sometimes so metrics reflect subtle quality loss, not complete nonsense
nina: ops question: will CI/blocking alerts be noisy? we need a daily digest + one-off pager only for T_high breaches
tara: agree. add alerting tiers: `synthetic-warning` -> daily digest; `synthetic-fail` -> oncall pager. tie pager to canary owner list
anjan: curious about maintenance: how do we evolve the synthetic corpus? periodic refresh cadence?
tara: cadence = quarterly, plus automated seed injection when we detect a new failure pattern in production post-mortem
frank: small ask: add a field in quant profiles: `synthetic_check_profile_version` so we can trace which synthetic set triggered the rejection
nina: good for audit. also make sure to log proof artifacts (sample, model outputs, diff) in S3 with retention 90d
tara: i'll draft a short RFC addendum with the config schema and example canary run output. want review from runtime + tooling
anjan: i'll take a pass on runtime integration
frank: i'll prototype the mutator and synthetic seed repo
nina: i'll scope alerting and Dedicated opt-in UI + billing note
deploy-bot: canary-run scheduled: model-family: small-bert, run-id: synthetic-probe-001, status: queued :gear:
tara: thanks all — will post the RFC addendum by EOD and link back here :thumbsup:
